findings.title: Restricted-mode tests pass for wrong reason, sanitize never called
findings.problem: test_create_new_restricted_mode_inline_servers_raises does not set mock_assistant_template.validate_fields.return_value = '', so MagicMock's truthy default return triggers ValidationException at the validate_fields() gate before sanitize_for_save() is reached. test_update_restricted_mode_inline_servers_raises has the same issue: mock_assistant_template._validate_mcp_server_names() is not set to return None, so its truthy MagicMock fires first. In both tests, mock_sanitize.side_effect is configured but sanitize_for_save() is never actually called.
findings.impact: Restricted-mode fail-fast via sanitize_for_save() (REQ-2.6, AC-4) is entirely unverified. A regression that silently skips or swallows the sanitize call in restricted mode would not be caught by these tests — they would continue to pass.
findings.recommendation: In test_create_new_restricted_mode_inline_servers_raises, add mock_assistant_template.validate_fields.return_value = '' before the pytest.raises assertion, then assert mock_sanitize.assert_called_once_with([_MCP_SERVER_A]) after to confirm the restricted-mode path ran. In test_update_restricted_mode_inline_servers_raises, add mock_assistant_template._validate_mcp_server_names.return_value = None and assert mock_sanitize.assert_called_once_with([_MCP_SERVER_A]).
